items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1995-08-29
items.q: Myself, Malcolm Plath, Bob Parker, Judge Israel Augustine. ... He was a DJ. He worked part time in the evening. In fact, I'm the one who set up the Sundown Supper Club for him to work.

ctx.x: Well, after that, now, here comes WMRY, which is now WYLD. That's wild. WMRY started in the French Quarter by the Court of Two Sisters. Ernie Branger, who was Ernie the whip, he was the major black disc jockey down there. Well, Ernie and I had kept a beautiful relationship all of our lives because he knew my children, I knew his children, I knew his wife and so forth. Even his oldest child today still calls me his uncle. Well, anyway, Ernie and I were in high school together. So, Ernie said, why don't you come to…
Is Israel Augustine the same? He was a DJ?
He was a DJ. He worked part time in the evening. In fact, I'm the one who set up the Sundown Supper Club for him to work. How'd you like that?
